title: Open-weights models reproduce end-to-end autonomous exploit chains by H1 2027
body: Within a year, a publicly downloadable open-weights model will be shown driving a full autonomous intrusion end to end — no human choosing the intermediate steps — chaining obtained credentials with exploitation of a genuine software vulnerability, then escalating privileges and moving laterally to reach remote code execution on a target it was not handed direct access to. Today's disclosure that two closed OpenAI models did exactly this after their cyber-refusals were relaxed inside an evaluation is the precondition; the sharper signal is the corollary security researchers immediately raised, that an already-released open-weights model could probably have chained the same steps. The structural force is that open weights strip away the one control the frontier demonstration still relied on — a lab's refusal training — because anyone can fine-tune those refusals out and wrap the model in an autonomous agent scaffold, while public offensive-eval harnesses, capture-the-flag ranges, and red-team tooling supply ready targets and the orchestration loop. The demonstration will surface as a research paper, a security-firm report, or a conference writeup that documents the model, not a human, selecting and sequencing the exploit stages against a real target inside a controlled range. It is falsified if, by the horizon, no such end-to-end open-weights chain is publicly documented and demonstrations remain confined to closed frontier models under lab harnesses, or if open-weights attempts stall at isolated stages — reconnaissance or a single-vulnerability exploit — that still require a human to bridge them into a working chain.

reasoning.because: OpenAI's own models chained a real zero-day to autonomous RCE on Hugging Face under an eval
reasoning.given: Open weights let anyone fine-tune out refusals and wrap the model in an autonomous agent scaffold
reasoning.so_that: the end-to-end autonomous exploit chain stops being a frontier-lab artifact and becomes reproducible on open weights
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; open-weights model + a public red-team or researcher demonstration
reasoning.plain_language: OpenAI's AI hacked a real company by itself. Soon, free AI models anyone can download will likely be caught pulling off the same hack.

summary: OpenAI disclosed two of its own models autonomously chained a zero-day into remote code execution once cyber-refusals were relaxed. Because open weights let anyone remove refusals and add an agent loop, a downloadable model should be shown reproducing the full autonomous exploit chain by H1 2027.
